summary:
RESEARCH ONLY. Nothing was downloaded, bought, installed or signed up for, and the repo was not edited. Sources are web pages and licence texts read on 2026-10-17. Figures marked 'estimate' are my inference, not sourced.

HEADLINE
1. Shooting real Ontario plants is the only route that gives species-true, cultivar-true and licence-clean visual data for all 26 species. The photos belong to Golden Maple, so they can ship to a public site and repo, but anyone can extract them, as with any web asset.
2. On its own, capture does not make a plant look photoreal. The best real-time plants (Megascans, SpeedTree-style) are built from scanned atlases placed on modelled geometry. The photos fix the leaf. The 3D build still decides the silhouette.
3. Raw photogrammetry fails on most foliage. Gaussian splats look the most photographic but are a poor fit for DeckCraft at runtime:
   - lighting is baked into the capture and cannot be relit;
   - splats cannot receive shadows;
   - they do not appear in the path-traced Photo mode;
   - the Spark runtime adds about 910 KB gzip;
   - phone splat budgets are only 1–1.5M splats in total.
4. Cut-out photo impostors are photographic from fixed eye-level cameras and very cheap on phones. They go flat up close and their lighting is baked.

RECOMMENDED COMBINATION (for the planner)
- (a) Species atlases shot on a light table and backdrop: leaves, needle and scale sprays, petals and flower heads, seed heads, grass blades and bark. These replace the SVG masks and CC0 photos in the current procedural plan.
- (b) Whole-plant multi-angle photos, plus an optional splat of each specimen. These are offline references: to measure the crown envelope and density, to run a side-by-side photo-match check at the Corner/Front/bed cameras, and to bake LOD2 impostors.
- (c) Photogrammetry with RealityScan or Meshroom, only for bark, trunk flares and the dense clipped shells (boxwood, yew, Smaragd).
- (d) No runtime splats in v1. At most, a later high-tier 'hero plant' experiment.

PILOT FIRST (before the first hard frost)
- Time window: Toronto Pearson's average first frost is about Oct 1–10, and Hamilton's is listed at Oct 28.
- Shoot these now: emerald cedar (flat sprays, easiest atlas), boxwood (before winter bronzing), Karl Foerster grass (tan plumes) and one blue spruce.
- Build them end to end and run the photo-match test. Decide go or no-go before committing to the summer 2027 sessions.
- Deciduous summer foliage cannot be shot until June 2027. Keep the interim procedural or CC0 assets until then. Species are picked at render time, so no data migration is needed.

SHOOT PLAN, 26 SPECIES (southern Ontario, zone 5; season windows are estimates from horticultural norms)
Now, mid-October until hard frost:
- Full capture of the evergreens: white pine (choose green outer sprigs; inner needles drop in autumn), Colorado blue spruce, Smaragd, yew (red arils on female plants now), and boxwood before it bronzes.
- All three grasses in their autumn form: Karl Foerster tan plumes, little bluestem copper stems with silver tufts, switchgrass gold with open panicles.
- Autumn-variant leaf atlases: sugar maple, red maple, serviceberry, redbud (yellow), dogwood, spirea, ninebark and lilac.
- Seed heads: coneflower and Rudbeckia cones, bergamot heads, tan Annabelle heads, rose-coloured panicle hydrangea heads, redbud pods and ostrich fern fertile fronds.
- Bark of all trees.
- Hosta and daylily are already yellowing, so leave them for June.

November to March:
- Leaf-off branch structure of the maples, serviceberry, redbud and lilac.
- Red-osier dogwood red stems (at their peak).
- Ninebark peeling bark.
- Bark photogrammetry, and pipeline testing indoors.

Late April to May 2027:
- Blooms: serviceberry (late April to early May), redbud (mid-May), lilac (mid to late May; a roughly 2-week window).
- Red maple flowers (March to April) and fiddleheads.
- Nurseries restock in this period.

June 2027:
- Mature summer leaves of every deciduous species.
- Hosta (best before slug damage), full ostrich fern fronds.
- Catmint and salvia first flush, ninebark and spirea flowers.
- Karl Foerster pink plumes.
- Annabelle heads open in late June.

July to August 2027:
- Coneflower, Rudbeckia, bergamot (shoot early, before mildew), daylily.
- Hosta scapes, Annabelle white heads, panicle hydrangea white or lime heads.
- Switchgrass haze, little bluestem blue foliage, salvia rebloom.

Nursery and location notes:
- In October, nursery stock is end-of-season. Perennials are cut back or tired; woody stock is still available.
- Connon's Waterdown home-gardener hours are listed as Mon–Sat 9–6. A Landscape Ontario profile says Sheridan's Kitchener store is open year-round.
- Nursery sizes are juvenile: #1 perennials are 15–25 cm rosettes, and trees are 50–60 mm caliper. They are fine for leaves and flowers, but established habit has to come from job sites, client gardens (with consent) or public gardens. Royal Botanical Gardens requires a paid permit for professional photography.

PER-SPECIES PROTOCOL (time per visit is an estimate)
- A. Atlas, 25–35 min:
  - Cut 15–25 specimens: three leaf sizes, sun and shade leaves, 3–5 sprays, 3–5 flower or seed heads. Shoot within 1–2 h; Megascans notes plants 'die very fast once unrooted or otherwise dissected'.
  - 3–5 layouts on an LED light pad, under glass if the material curls.
  - Per layout, about 12–15 frames:
    - backlit only, for alpha and translucency;
    - cross-polarized front light, for albedo;
    - parallel-polarized, for gloss;
    - 4–8 raking-light positions plus a chrome ball, for photometric normals;
    - a ColorChecker frame for each lighting setup.
  - 3D flowers and heads: 6–8 angles each on a blue or white backdrop.
- B. Whole plant, 15–20 min per specimen, 2–3 specimens per species:
  - On a turntable, in still air: 3 elevation rings (about 0°, 20°, 45°) × 24 stops, plus a top view. Include a scale rod and the ColorChecker.
  - Optionally 150–300 frames, or a 2–3 min orbit video, for a splat.
  - Trees: 8 compass views from 2–3× the tree's height away, crown close-ups, and a leaf-off visit.
- C. Bark and stems, about 10 min: 40–80 overlapping frames of a 1 m section.

Totals (estimates):
- 1–1.5 h of shooting per species per season visit, 1–3 visits each.
- About 45–70 h of shooting over 2026–27.
- About 10–15k frames. Keep RAW only for colour-critical frames and JPEG/HEIF for the photogrammetry and splat frames: about 50–100 GB, kept off the repo and off C:.
- Processing about 1–2 h per species once the pipeline scripts exist.

WHAT THE PIPELINE DOES WITH CAPTURES
1. RAW to linear: darktable colour-calibration fitted to the ColorChecker. darktable does not read ProRAW, so ProRAW goes through Adobe DNG Converter first.
2. Alpha: a luminance key from the backlit frame, or a chroma key. Fallback is rembg with birefnet-general (MIT), never rembg's default bria-rmbg.
3. Maps: albedo (cross-polarized), translucency (backlit), normals (Meshroom PhotometricStereo; Materialize as fallback), roughness (parallel minus cross-polarized).
4. Pack and colour-dilate the atlases, then encode KTX2 with sharp plus a basis encoder.
5. Feed the atlases and the measured crown envelope into the procedural species generator, and build LOD0, LOD1 and LOD2.
6. Bake hemi-octahedral impostors for LOD2 (agargaro/octahedral-impostor, MIT, or an in-repo bake).
7. Photo-match QA: render each species from the same camera as its reference photo.
8. Provenance manifest. check-landscape-objects.ts currently hard-codes Poly Haven CC0 and must accept a 'project-owned capture' record.
9. Strip EXIF/GPS. Never commit the raw sources.

GEAR (list prices; buying needs owner approval)
- ColorChecker Passport Photo 2: US$119 list, US$89.25 sale (calibrite.com). Classic Mini about US$74.
- A3 LED light pad: Huion A3 AU$90–99 in Australia (about C$80–90), or generic pads at about C$40–70 (estimate).
- Linear polarizer film sheet: about US$15–40 (estimate). Edmund Optics XP42 is cut to size on quote. Film can also be salvaged from an old LCD.
- Phone polarizer: Moment AntiGlare CPL II US$75 (needs a Moment case, iPhone 15+), or a generic clip-on at about US$15–30 (estimate).
- Neewer 5×7 ft blue/green collapsible backdrop: US$69.99.
- Two CRI 95+ LED panels: about US$40–100 each (estimate).
- Tripod with Bluetooth remote: about C$30–60 (estimate).
- Turntable: lazy susan C$20–40, or heavy-duty motorized about US$60–200 (estimate).
- Small items: chrome ball bearing, glass pane, grey card, scale rod, about C$30 (estimate).
- Total: about C$350–700.
- Software: the free path is $0. RealityScan is free below US$1M group revenue; above that it is US$1,250 per seat per year.
- Paid options: Metashape Standard US$179 (perpetual); Polycam Basic US$150/yr; KIRI Pro US$79.99/yr; Postshot Indie (price not shown on the fetched page); Substance 3D Texturing US$24.99/mo (2025 price; may not be sold to new buyers in 2026).

LICENCE TRAPS FOUND
- rembg's default model, RMBG-2.0, 'requires a paid agreement for commercial use'.
- The INRIA 3DGS code, and the 2DGS and SuGaR repos that carry the same Gaussian-Splatting License, are non-commercial.
- Postshot Free is listed as 'Non-commercial use' and cannot export radiance fields.
- Polycam ToS §5.2 requires 'attribution to the Company for any public display' of Models, and §5.1 conflicts with it ('internal use only').
- Niantic Spatial (Scaniverse) §6.3 takes a perpetual licence over your content that includes AI training, even though you own the Output (§6.2).
- Metashape demo and trial outputs 'shall not be used for commercial purposes'.
- Depth Anything V2 Base and Large are CC-BY-NC; only Small is Apache-2.0.
- No licence problem: RealityScan EULA §6 claims nothing in your content; Meshroom MPL-2.0; COLMAP BSD; gsplat, nerfstudio and Brush Apache-2.0; Spark, SuperSplat, spz and splat-transform MIT.

OWNER DECISIONS NEEDED
- Approve the gear budget.
- Confirm Golden Maple's group revenue against RealityScan's US$1M threshold.
- Nursery photography permission (outreach is the owner's).
- Job-site client consent.
- Which cultivars to capture: those Golden Maple installs most, e.g. hosta and daylily cultivars, ninebark colour.
- Asset licence notice for the public repo (e.g. all rights reserved).
- Default render season (summer) and whether autumn variants ship.
- Approval to install darktable, Meshroom, RealityScan, Brush and Blender add-ons.
- Whether to run the pilot now.

routes.name: R1. Light-table and backdrop photo atlases of each species
routes.what: The owner photographs cut specimens of each species on an LED light pad, plus a blue or white backdrop for 3D parts, with a ColorChecker in frame. Parts: leaves, conifer needle and scale sprays, flower heads and petals, seed heads, grass blades and plumes, and bark. Lighting: cross-polarized for albedo, parallel-polarized for gloss, backlit for alpha and translucency, and 4-8 raking lights plus a chrome ball for photometric-stereo normals. The pipeline turns these into species-true alpha-cut atlases (albedo, alpha, translucency, normal, roughness). The atlases go onto the leaf, needle and petal cards of the existing procedural or hand-built geometry, replacing the SVG masks and the CC0/iNaturalist photos in PLAN.md. This is the same method behind scanned foliage atlases from Megascans, Poliigon and Textures.com.
routes.species_coverage: All 26 at species level, and at cultivar level when shot from labelled stock ('Smaragd', 'Annabelle', 'Karl Foerster', 'Walker's Low', 'May Night', 'Diabolo' and so on). Easiest (flat parts): both maples, serviceberry, redbud, ninebark, red-osier dogwood, both hydrangeas' leaves, lilac, spirea, hosta, daylily, Thuja scale sprays, yew two-ranked sprays, boxwood sprigs, ostrich fern pinnae, the three grasses' blades and plumes, and catmint and salvia leaves. Harder: white pine (5-needle bundles about 10 cm long must be laid flat under glass), blue spruce (radial needles, so shoot sprig tips from above and accept some flattening), and 3D inflorescences (coneflower cone, Rudbeckia dome, Annabelle globe, panicle hydrangea cone, lilac panicle, bergamot head). These need 6-8 angle shots on the backdrop instead of flat atlas cells. Season limits apply; see the summary.
routes.realism: Each leaf, needle, petal and bark texel is photographic and correct for the species. That covers colour, venation, edge shape and translucency, the details that betray Burkea africana or fir cards today. Plant-level realism still depends on the branch and card geometry and on shading: atlases alone do not fix silhouettes, clumping or card scale. Industry bar: Megascans builds 'one atlas including every component the plant is made out of' (https://80.lv/articles/billy-lundevall-creating-content-for-megascans), and its scanner records albedo, alpha, gloss, normal and translucency in one sequence. Poliigon leaf atlases are photometric-stereo captures (https://www.poliigon.com/texture/maple-leaves-texture-atlas/9856, via search snippet). Henry Kelly's ivy was shot on a blue backdrop and processed from DNG (https://www.adobe.com/learn/substance-3d-designer/web/creating-ivy-from-scanned-data-with-substance-designer). Polycount practitioners recommend shooting on a lightbox for alphas and translucency, and cross-polarized light for albedo and gloss (https://polycount.com/discussion/comment/2686865, via search snippet). Expected result (estimate): close to photographic in path-traced Photo-mode stills at the Corner/Front cameras, given good geometry. Real-time phone views will read as high-end game foliage, not indistinguishable from a photo.
routes.licence:
Project-owned photographs: Golden Maple holds copyright and no third-party licence applies. They may be committed to the public repo or served from any origin. Extraction cannot be prevented, so add a rights notice (for example all rights reserved) for the asset folder and keep RAW masters off the repo.

Tool licences do not attach to outputs:
- darktable GPL-3.0, GIMP GPL-3, Materialize GPL-3.
- Meshroom MPL-2.0 (https://meshroom.org) has a PhotometricStereo node: 'Reconstruction using Photometric Stereo. The lighting conditions are assumed to be known.' (https://meshroom.readthedocs.io/en/latest/generated/meshroom.nodes.aliceVision.PhotometricStereo.PhotometricStereo.html). Its LightingCalibration node estimates the light 'using spheres placed in the scene'.
- rembg is MIT, but its README warns 'Model weights carry their own licenses, independent of rembg's MIT license', and its default bria-rmbg (RMBG-2.0) 'requires a paid agreement for commercial use' (https://github.com/danielgatis/rembg). Use -m birefnet-general instead (BiRefNet, MIT: https://github.com/ZhengPeng7/BiRefNet), or deterministic backlight and chroma keys.
- Depth Anything V2: 'Depth-Anything-V2-Small model is under the Apache-2.0 license'; 'Depth-Anything-V2-Base/Large/Giant models are under the CC-BY-NC-4.0 license' (https://github.com/DepthAnything/Depth-Anything-V2).
routes.cost:
Gear about C$250-600, with owner approval for each purchase:
- Calibrite ColorChecker Passport Photo 2: US$119 list, US$89.25 sale (https://calibrite.com/us/product/colorchecker-passport-photo-2/).
- A3 LED light pad: Huion A3 AU$90-99 at PB Tech (https://www.pbtech.com/au/product/KEYHUN4002/Huion-A3-LED-Light-Pad); generic pads about C$40-70 (estimate).
- Linear polarizer film: Edmund Optics cuts XP42 to size on quote, with 12.5 mm discs at US$11.95 (https://www.edmundoptics.com/p/125mm-dia-linear-polarizing-film-xp42-18/45833/). Generic A4 sheets about US$15-30 (estimate). Free if salvaged from an old LCD (https://www.pix-pro.com/blog/cross-polarization).
- Phone polarizer: Moment AntiGlare CPL QuickLock II US$75, needs a Moment case and iPhone 15+ (https://www.shopmoment.com/products/antiglare-cpl-quicklock-filter-ii); generic clip-on CPL about US$15-30 (estimate).
- Two LED panels with CRI 95+: about US$40-100 each (estimate).
- Glass pane, chrome ball and grey card: about C$30 (estimate).

Software is $0 on the free path. Optional paid: Substance 3D Texturing (Sampler) US$24.99/mo or US$249.88/yr per Adobe's 2025 announcement (https://blog.adobe.com/en/publish/2025/02/20/substance-3d-innovations-pricing-updates); 2026 availability to new buyers is unclear.
routes.owner_actions:
- Approve the gear purchases.
- Confirm the phone model and RAW support. iPhone ProRAW needs Adobe DNG Converter for darktable; Android DNG gain maps can shift colour (https://discuss.pixls.us/t/samsung-s26-ultra-dng-calibration-yellow-tint-cct-invalid-error/59401).
- Arrange cuttings from own or job-site plants with client consent, or from nursery stock with permission. Buying a plant to cut is a purchase.
- Run 25-35 min atlas sessions per species per season visit.
- Decide which cultivars represent 'hosta', 'daylily', 'ninebark' and so on.
- Choose the asset rights notice.
- Approve installing darktable, Meshroom and Blender.
routes.web_fit:
- Atlases: 1k-2k cells packed into 3-4 shared atlases, KTX2 (ETC1S colour/alpha, UASTC normals), about 0.5-1.5 MB per species (estimate). The prior plan estimates about 2.7 MiB of KTX2 for the 31-plant demo bed.
- Geometry: unchanged from the procedural plan: tree LOD0 about 15-25k tris, shrubs 2-8k, perennials 1-4k; LOD1, then a baked LOD2.
- Compatibility: works with alpha-to-coverage (MSAA tiers), GTAO, shadow maps, Neutral tone mapping and three-gpu-pathtracer stills. No new runtime dependency.
- Effort: high. It needs a capture-processing script chain (darktable CLI, keying, photometric stereo, atlas packing) and art direction. The geometry work from PLAN.md is still needed.
routes.risks:
- Wilting: shoot within 1-2 h of cutting.
- Colour drift between sessions and phones: re-shoot the ColorChecker for each lighting setup; avoid in-phone HDR processing.
- 3D needles and inflorescences flatten on the pad.
- Polarizer alignment with a phone is approximate.
- Season windows: deciduous summer foliage only June-August 2027.
- The atlases do not fix geometry, which stays the main realism bottleneck.
- EXIF/GPS in source photos: never commit originals.
- Mislabelled nursery cultivars.
- check-landscape-objects.ts rejects non-Poly Haven provenance until updated.

routes.name: R2. Whole-plant cut-out photography for billboards and view-dependent photo impostors
routes.what:
Shoot each specimen against a blue or green backdrop at known angles:
- Potted nursery stock on a turntable: 3 elevation rings of 24 stops each, plus top views.
- In-ground specimens: walk-around shots.

Cut the frames out to alpha and use them as:
- (a) ArchViz-style 2D or cross billboards;
- (b) hemi-octahedral or flipbook impostor atlases for LOD2 and far views;
- (c) ground-truth photo-match references for judging LOD0 at the Corner/Front/bed cameras.

Note that Lumion's and Twinmotion's own vegetation is 3D. Their 2D cut-outs are mainly people; custom PNG billboards are a user feature.
routes.species_coverage: All 26 as photographed. The 23 shrubs, perennials and grasses suit a turntable when in pots. The five large trees (sugar maple, red maple, white pine, blue spruce, and serviceberry/redbud at landscape size) cannot be turntabled: field shots only, with wind and background clutter. Their impostors are better baked from the 3D model. Nursery sizes are juvenile: #1 perennials are 15-25 cm rosettes and trees are 50-60 mm caliper (botany research). Established habit therefore needs in-ground specimens on job sites or in public gardens.
routes.realism:
Seen from a captured angle it is literally a photograph, so it can be indistinguishable at fixed eye-level views and in the distance. It fails when the camera orbits close (flat card, no internal parallax), from uncaptured elevations, and under DeckCraft's directional sun and shadows, because overcast light is baked in.

Precedents:
- Quick Garden Plants (Blender) builds photo billboards from 'my own unique photographs, personally captured in my private garden' and warns 'Avoid extreme close-ups' (https://superhivemarket.com/products/quick_garden_plants/docs; US$3 / Pro US$7).
- three.js octahedral-impostor forest: a commenter saw 'lines visible on the sprite if you look closely' (https://discourse.threejs.org/t/a-forest-of-octahedral-impostors/85735).
- Twinmotion: 'Cutout: Static 2D human characters and groups of characters.' (https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/twinmotion/twinmotion-assets-in-the-twinmotion-library).
- Lumion supports custom 2D cut-outs through the Character Billboard object or a Billboard Material (https://support.lumion.com/hc/en-us/articles/360003475313).
routes.licence: Project-owned photographs; no third-party terms. Impostor runtime library: agargaro/octahedral-impostor, MIT (https://github.com/agargaro/octahedral-impostor; GitHub API licence MIT). Keying tools as in R1. The same notes apply on extraction from a public repo and on keeping masters off the repo.
routes.cost:
Same base gear as R1, plus:
- Neewer 5x7 ft 2-in-1 collapsible blue/green backdrop, 'From $69.99' (https://neewer.com/products/lighting-studio-66600789); blue/grey version US$59.99.
- Turntable: lazy susan about C$20-40 for #1-#3 pots; motorised heavy-duty model about US$60-200 for #5-#15 shrubs (estimate).
- Optional pop-up shelter or garage space to block wind.
routes.owner_actions:
- Access to nursery stock, by permission or by approved purchase. A good fit is to capture plants bought for an upcoming client install before planting.
- A windless indoor or garage space.
- 15-20 min per specimen, 2-3 specimens per species for variety.
- Field visits to mature specimens with consent. Royal Botanical Gardens says permits 'are required for any professional photography session' (https://secure.rbg.ca/7103/7120, via search snippet).
routes.web_fit:
- Per species: one 2048x2048 atlas (4096 for a hero plant) holding an 8x8 hemi-octahedral grid of 256x256 views, KTX2 about 0.5-2 MB (estimate).
- Runtime cost: 2 triangles per instance. This is the ideal constrained-tier LOD2 and suits the 273-plant estate on phones.
- Photo mode: a camera-facing alpha-tested card can be path-traced for a still. three-gpu-pathtracer supports only MeshStandardMaterial and MeshPhysicalMaterial (https://github.com/gkjohnson/three-gpu-pathtracer); alpha-test behaviour still needs checking.
- Shadows: card-shaped unless a depth channel or proxy is used. Photos give no depth or normals; Depth Anything V2 Small (Apache-2.0) could estimate them, quality unverified.
routes.risks:
- Baked overcast light against the scene's sun.
- Exposure and colour differences between azimuths: lock exposure and white balance, shoot RAW.
- Plant sway on a turntable. A 3DF Zephyr forum tip: use a turntable with 'minimal vibration', keep it 'rotating continuously', and use strobe or very fast shutter (https://3dflow.net/forums/forum/3df-zephyr-forum-english/8274-any-tipps-for-reconstructing-leafs-plants).
- Backdrop colour spill on fine grass panicles: use backlight or a light backdrop.
- View-snapping or interpolation seams.
- Juvenile forms may not match DeckCraft's design sizes.
- Not usable for close-up hero views.

routes.name: R3. Photogrammetry with RealityScan 2.x desktop (formerly RealityCapture)
routes.species_coverage:
- Good: bark of sugar maple, red maple, white pine and spruce (trunk), serviceberry and redbud stems, lilac canes, red-osier dogwood stems (colour), ninebark peeling bark.
- Usable as shells: boxwood, yew, Smaragd.
- Moderate: hosta (large leaves reconstruct, but edges come out thick and overlapping leaves blob together).
- Poor to fail: coneflower, Rudbeckia, bergamot, catmint, salvia, daylily (strap leaves partly), spirea, Annabelle and panicle hydrangea heads, ostrich fern (thin fronds), all three grasses, white pine and blue spruce foliage, ninebark and dogwood canopies, and every whole tree (size, wind, unreachable upper crown).
routes.realism:
Bark and trunk scans are photoreal. Foliage reconstructs as thickened, holed shells that look sculpted up close. Examples:
- 'Hosta plantaginea Small (Raw Scan)', 'using RealityScan', 881,916 faces (https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/eb09bec9021c4e8fbe3d61585eb1a2b5).
- Adenium 'Scanned with Reality Capture', 999,976 faces, with Polycam photogrammetry and splat comparisons linked in its description (https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/9052bd0495d44d138251f5efdf9a432d).
- 'Snow bush' photogrammetry, 800,633 faces (https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/24cd15da71ca4cdcb18956c2682bda34).
- 'Plane tree trunk', 711,264 faces (https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/3bb1c5445e22498db449a296b34620a5).

Plant literature: 'thin leaves, fine stems, self-occlusion, non-rigid and slowly changing structures make plants difficult for three-dimensional scanning' (search snippet from https://arxiv.org/html/2504.16840v1). A 2026 drone study: 'Wind speed significantly influenced the canopy height reconstructions' (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2607.07905).
routes.licence:
RealityScan EULA (https://www.realityscan.com/eula):
- §6: 'Your use of the Software does not grant to Licensor any right, title, or interest in any of the content that you produce using the Software or any of the content that you import into the Software.'
- §2(b)(i): 'During any period that you, together with any entities in your corporate group, have generated less than $1,000,000 USD in gross revenue over the last 12 months, the Seat subscription requirement will not apply to your Users.'
- §1.1 limits only the Sample Datasets: 'you may only use Sample Datasets for non-commercial purposes.'

Licence page (https://www.realityscan.com/license): above the threshold, '$1250' per seat per year. Outputs are project-owned and fine for public web and repo use.
routes.cost: $0 if Golden Maple's group revenue is under US$1M over the last 12 months. Otherwise US$1,250 per seat per year (https://www.realityscan.com/license).
routes.owner_actions:
- Confirm the revenue threshold.
- Approve the install through the Epic Games Launcher or Developer Portal. That needs an Epic account, which is an owner sign-up.
- Shoot bark at about 40-80 frames per 1 m section, on overcast days or with cross-polarized flash.
- For clipped shrubs, shoot indoors or in still air.
routes.web_fit:
- Raw output is 0.5-2M faces with 8k textures. Each asset needs retopology or decimation to about 2-20k tris plus normal and AO bakes to 1k-2k KTX2.
- Bark: crop to tileable 1k sets of about 1-3 MB at 1k JPG, similar to Poly Haven bark (estimate).
- The repo has no gltf-transform or meshoptimizer yet; one or both must be added as build-time tools.
- Outputs are ordinary meshes, so they work with shadows, GTAO, MSAA and the path tracer.
routes.risks:
- Baked light in the albedo: use overcast light or cross-polarization, or de-light.
- Holes and thick shells on foliage; wind.
- Masks needed on busy nursery backgrounds.
- Large processing and storage.
- Revenue-threshold compliance. The terms are a seat subscription, so a future EULA change could alter the free tier.

routes.name: R4. Other desktop photogrammetry: Meshroom/AliceVision, COLMAP, Agisoft Metashape
routes.what:
Alternatives or complements to R3:
- Meshroom (2025.1, MPL-2.0): full photogrammetry plus PhotometricStereo and LightingCalibration nodes, which turn R1 multi-light leaf shots into normal and albedo maps.
- COLMAP (BSD): camera poses for splat training in R5.
- Agisoft Metashape: a commercial photogrammetry tool favoured for cross-polarized texture scanning. Grzegorz Baran built a dry-grass ground material from '201 - 32Mpx cross-polarised images' in Metashape (https://gbaran.artstation.com/projects/bl44lk).
routes.species_coverage: Same as R3: bark, trunks, ground, clipped shells, partial hosta. Meshroom photometric stereo also serves R1 normals for all 26 species' flat parts.
routes.realism: Reconstruction quality is similar to RealityScan on foliage, with the same failure modes. Photometric stereo gives real micro-normals (veins, needle ridges) and is how commercial leaf atlases get their normals. Example: an elm atlas 'built from several light positions' (https://www.poliigon.com/texture/elm-leaves-texture-atlas/9854, via search snippet).
routes.licence:
Meshroom: MPL-2.0 (https://meshroom.org footer links mozilla.org/MPL/2.0). COLMAP: BSD-3 (https://github.com/colmap/colmap). Neither claims any rights in outputs.

Agisoft Metashape Standard 2.0 EULA (https://www.agisoft.com/pdf/metashape_eula.pdf):
- §2.1.1 Node-Locked: 'for commercial and non-commercial purposes'.
- §2.2.1 Trial and §2.3 Demo: 'including any materials created with the help of it shall not be used for commercial purposes'.
- §3(e): 'You may not use the PROGRAM in any kind of automated processing service'.
- No clause claims ownership of output.
routes.cost:
- Meshroom and COLMAP: $0.
- Metashape Standard US$179 node-locked, Professional US$3,499 node-locked; floating licences by quote (https://www.agisoft.com/buy/online-store/).
- The Metashape demo or trial cannot be used to make shippable assets.
routes.owner_actions:
- Approve installs. Meshroom needs a CUDA GPU; the RTX 5070 is fine.
- If Metashape is wanted, approve the US$179 purchase.
- Buy a chrome ball bearing for light calibration.
routes.web_fit: Same as R3 for meshes. Photometric-stereo normals feed straight into the R1 atlases at no runtime cost.
routes.risks:
- Meshroom is slower and less polished than RealityScan.
- Photometric stereo needs fixed camera and leaves with only the light moving. Areas shadowed in every shot give no data: one Polycount user found areas 'shadowed in all eight source pictures', which left blurred albedo (search snippet, https://polycount.com/discussion/comment/2686999/).
- Metashape licence is per device.

routes.name: R5. Phone cloud capture apps: Polycam, KIRI Engine, RealityScan Mobile, Luma
routes.what: Phone apps that capture and process in the cloud (Polycam, KIRI, RealityScan Mobile, Luma), or on the device (Scaniverse, covered under R6). They are fast in the field: a 2-5 min orbit gives a mesh or splat, useful for scouting and reference. They were judged against the public-web rule.
routes.species_coverage: As R3 for meshes. As R6 for splats, which are better on fine foliage.
routes.realism: Phone-app meshes are lower detail than desktop RealityScan. Fabbaloo found RealityScan Mobile's resolution 'quite poor' for faces (https://www.fabbaloo.com/news/hands-on-with-realityscan-part-2). Example: a Polycam photogrammetry capture and a Polycam splat of the same adenium, linked from https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/9052bd0495d44d138251f5efdf9a432d (poly.cam/capture/63845DA1-0581-442C-8B02-C77CD56E805B and poly.cam/capture/CD562C7C-14BC-45AE-9ABB-FC36555EA2C7).
routes.licence:
Polycam Terms of Service, last revised April 25 2025 (https://poly.cam/legal/terms-of-service):
- §6.4: 'we do not claim any ownership in your Models or other elements of Your Content'.
- §5.2: 'you may copy, modify, publish, distribute, sublicense, commercialize, or otherwise use any Models' 'provided that you provide attribution to the Company for any public display of any such Models'.
- §5.1: 'We hereby permit you to use the Services for your internal use only.' This conflicts with §5.2.
- §6.5 grants Polycam a licence that is 'royalty free, transferable, sub-licensable, worldwide and irrevocable', lasting 'for so long as Your Content is stored with us'.

Polycam privacy notice (https://poly.cam/privacy_policy): 'We may also license UGC to third parties to use for their own purposes, including training artificial intelligence models.' This is in the context of public content.

KIRI Engine: ToS not reviewed. RealityScan Mobile: processing runs on Epic servers, with export via Sketchfab per 2023 reviews (https://www.cgchannel.com/2023/06/epic-games-releases-realityscan-1-1); the current mobile terms were not found. Luma: Flythroughs was retired on 1 January 2026, and Luma's 3D capture future is unclear (https://radiancefields.com/luma-ai-to-sunset-flythroughs-on-january-1-2026).
routes.cost:
Polycam (https://poly.cam/pricing):
- Free: 10 photogrammetry captures, 150 images per capture.
- Basic: US$150/yr or US$30/mo.
- Business: US$400/user/yr.
- Enterprise: US$1,200/user/yr, 3-seat minimum.

KIRI Engine (https://www.kiriengine.app/pricing): Basic free; Pro US$79.99/yr or US$17.99/mo. 3DGS mesh-inclusive scans and featureless-object scans are Pro only.

RealityScan Mobile: free. Luma: not priced here.
routes.owner_actions:
- Accounts and sign-ups, and any subscription, are owner actions that need approval.
- If Polycam assets ship, decide how the site credits Polycam.
- Owner to read the KIRI and RealityScan Mobile terms.
routes.web_fit: Output is GLB/OBJ/PLY meshes or splats. They need the same decimation and baking as R3, or the same runtime as R6.
routes.risks:
- Cloud upload grants the vendor broad licences.
- Polycam attribution, plus the §5.1 versus §5.2 ambiguity.
- App lock-in and changing product lines: Polycam Pro is now 'Legacy Pro', and Luma has pivoted.
- Lower capture control than desktop tools.
- Recommendation: prefer local desktop processing (R3, R4, R6 with Brush or gsplat) for anything that ships.

routes.name: R6. Gaussian-splat capture and training of real plants
routes.what:
Capture each specimen as a 3D Gaussian splat (radiance field) from a phone: 150-300 photos or a 2-3 min orbit video, in still air, on overcast days or indoors. Options:
- Scaniverse: free, trains on the phone, exports PLY/SPZ.
- Polycam splats (Basic plan).
- Train locally on the RTX 5070 with Brush (Apache-2.0, WebGPU, any GPU) or gsplat/nerfstudio (Apache-2.0, CUDA), or Jawset Postshot.
- Clean up in SuperSplat (MIT) and convert with splat-transform (MIT) or spz (MIT).

This route covers capture only; the runtime is R7. Best uses: ground truth for photo-match QA, a source for rendering impostor views with alpha and depth, and measured crown envelopes and densities.
routes.species_coverage: The best capture method for fine foliage at shrub and perennial scale: grasses (plumes and haze), catmint, salvia, bergamot, coneflower, Rudbeckia, daylily, hosta, fern, spirea, ninebark, dogwood, both hydrangeas, lilac, boxwood, yew, Smaragd, and young spruce or pine. Trees (sugar maple, red maple, white pine, blue spruce, serviceberry and redbud at landscape size) are only partial: the upper crown cannot be reached without a pole or drone, and wind blurs it.
routes.realism:
The highest photographic fidelity of any capture route, especially for thin, fuzzy and translucent parts. LeafFit (Eurographics 2026, https://arxiv.org/html/2602.11577v1): '3DGS faithfully captures complex foliage', but its 'high memory footprint and lack of mesh topology make it incompatible with traditional game production workflows.' Examples:
- 'Tree - Scaniverse 3D Gaussian Splat ply', 279,884 splats (https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/6fa62a71aa184963a5082c4436e07920).
- 'Flower pot gaussian splat', 'Caputred on iPhone 14 Pro' (https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/7403595b202d43f5afc4c90655baf1f1).
- Polycam adenium splat (poly.cam/capture/CD562C7C-14BC-45AE-9ABB-FC36555EA2C7).

The capture's lighting is baked in permanently.
routes.licence:
- Scaniverse / Niantic Spatial ToS, modified February 20 2026 (https://www.nianticspatial.com/terms): §6.1 'Niantic Spatial does not claim ownership rights in User Content'; §6.2 'you own all right, title and interest in and to all Output generated in response to your User Content'; §6.3 grants Niantic a 'non-exclusive, worldwide, transferable, sub-licensable, royalty-free, perpetual' licence, including to train 'semantic and geospatial models and other artificial intelligence and machine learning algorithms and models'.
- Postshot (https://activation.jawset.com/shop/pricing): Free tier lists 'Non-commercial use' and only 'Export camera poses and points'. Indie adds 'Commercial use' and 'Export Radiance Fields in PLY, SPZ formats'.
- Brush: Apache-2.0 (https://github.com/ArthurBrussee/brush). gsplat: Apache-2.0 (https://github.com/nerfstudio-project/gsplat). nerfstudio: Apache-2.0. SuperSplat, splat-transform and spz: MIT.
- AVOID the original INRIA code (https://github.com/graphdeco-inria/gaussian-splatting/blob/main/LICENSE.md): 'The Software may be used "non-commercially", i.e., for research and/or evaluation purposes only.' and 'THE USER CANNOT USE, EXPLOIT OR DISTRIBUTE THE SOFTWARE FOR COMMERCIAL PURPOSES'. The 2DGS (hbb1/2d-gaussian-splatting) and SuGaR (Anttwo/SuGaR) LICENSE files carry the same 'Gaussian-Splatting License' header (checked 2026-10-17).
- Polycam: see R5.
routes.cost:
- Scaniverse, Brush, gsplat, nerfstudio, SuperSplat: $0.
- Postshot Indie: required for commercial use and export. The price did not render on the fetched pricing page (it showed placeholder EUR 0.00), so the owner must check it.
- Polycam Basic: US$150/yr.
- KIRI Pro: US$79.99/yr.
routes.owner_actions:
- 2-3 min orbit captures per specimen.
- Choose local training (Brush or gsplat, needs installs) or Scaniverse on-device, accepting Niantic's §6.3 licence including AI training.
- Approve any Postshot Indie or Polycam subscription.
- Note: gsplat on an RTX 50-series card may need a recent CUDA/PyTorch build. Brush uses WebGPU and avoids this.
routes.web_fit:
- Raw splats run 150k-1M per specimen. PLY with SH degree 3 is about 248 B/splat. SPZ is 'About 10x smaller than the PLY equivalent' (https://github.com/nianticlabs/spz). PlayCanvas SOG is '~15-20x smaller', with 4M splats in 42 MB, about 10.5 B/splat by my arithmetic (https://blog.playcanvas.com/playcanvas-open-sources-sog-format-for-gaussian-splatting/).
- So a 150-500k-splat shrub is about 1.6-5 MB as SOG (estimate).
- Offline, splats can be rendered from N directions with alpha and depth to bake R2-style impostors without the photos' framing problems.
- Training time per plant on the RTX 5070: about 10-40 min (estimate).
routes.risks:
- Wind and movement ruin captures.
- Floaters and background need cleanup.
- Baked light.
- Licence traps: Postshot Free, INRIA-derived code, Polycam attribution, Niantic AI-training licence.
- Mesh extraction from splats for foliage is research-grade. LeafFit tested mostly elliptic houseplant leaves; it states 'We do not store per-leaf meshes', and the code release is not confirmed.

routes.name: R7. Runtime library of splat plants in DeckCraft (Spark 2.x)
routes.what:
Ship captured plants as splats and render them inside the three.js scene with Spark (sparkjs.dev, World Labs). Alternatives were checked:
- mkkellogg GaussianSplats3D: 'no longer in active development'; its author recommends Spark; listed with 'Sub-optimal performance on mobile devices'; needs COOP/COEP headers for SharedArrayBuffer unless sharedMemoryForWorkers is false.
- three.js r186 native splats: WebGPU/TSL NodeMaterial only, 'SH0 only', 'no level of detail, no streaming', and on the dev branch. They do not fit the current WebGLRenderer pipeline.
routes.species_coverage: Whatever R6 captures: in practice the 21 shrub, perennial and grass species plus small conifers. Trees are partial.
routes.realism:
Up close, from captured viewpoints and under lighting that matches the capture, splats are the only real-time route that can pass for a photo. Inside DeckCraft they break the photoreal bar in other ways:
- No received shadows from the house or deck.
- No reaction to sun direction or time of day. Relighting is limited: 'Relighting is a modulation, so it cannot change hue or remove a shadow baked in at capture.' The GDGS team measured native lighting 'at 2.5 to 3.9x frame time before dropping it' (https://radiancefields.com/reconworldlab-adds-relighting-to-godot-gaussian-splats-in-gdgs-3.3.0).
- Splats do not appear in path-traced Photo-mode stills: three-gpu-pathtracer lists no splat or point primitive (https://github.com/gkjohnson/three-gpu-pathtracer).
- Babylon.js users report splat colour is 'diffuse + lighting baked' (https://forum.babylonjs.com/t/light-interacting-with-gaussians-in-gaussian-splatting-for-generating-shadows/58659).
routes.licence: Spark: MIT (https://github.com/sparkjsdev/spark; npm @sparkjsdev/spark 2.3.1 'license: MIT', peerDependencies three >=0.180.0, dependency fflate). Captured content is project-owned (R6).
routes.cost: $0 licence. It does carry a big engineering and performance cost (see web_fit).
routes.owner_actions: None now. A later go-ahead would be needed for a high-tier 'hero plant' experiment.
routes.web_fit:
Bundle:
- @sparkjsdev/spark 2.3.1 is 2,620,859 B minified and 910,111 B gzip (bundlephobia). That is about 38x the current 23.8 KB-gzip lazy Landscape3D chunk, so it must be its own lazy chunk.

LoD and budgets (https://sparkjs.dev/docs/lod-getting-started/): per-frame splat budget '1M for Android, 1.5M for iOS, and 2.5M for desktop'. The performance page gives 'Android phone: 1-2 million splats' and 'iPhone: 1-3 million splats' (https://sparkjs.dev/docs/performance/).
- 31-plant demo bed: about 32-48k splats per plant on phones (soft).
- 273-plant showcase: about 4-9k per plant, i.e. blobs, unless LoD concentrates splats on near plants.

Memory: PackedSplats take 'exactly 16 bytes per splat' (https://sparkjs.dev/docs/packed-splats/). A loaded PackedSplats 'can then be used as an input source for multiple SplatMesh instances' (https://sparkjs.dev/docs/loading-splats/), so instancing per species works, at about 2.4-8 MB GPU per unique species (estimate). Spark 2.0 uses a 16M-splat default page pool.

Pipeline conflicts:
- AA: 'WebGL anti-aliasing doesn't improve Gaussian Splatting rendering and significantly reduces performance', which clashes with the MSAA tiers.
- depthWrite: 'may produce undesirable results because most of the Gsplat is transparent', so GTAO and depth-based post ignore the splats.
- Transparency: splats render in the transparent pass by default; sorting against the frameless glass railing is a likely artefact source.
- On-demand rendering works through onDirty, but 'each one needs another render to become visible' and 'The sort order lags the render by at least one frame' (https://sparkjs.dev/docs/system-design/).
- Tone mapping and colour-space interaction with Neutral tone mapping is undocumented and would need a test.

Shadows: none built in. Casting only via a hidden proxy mesh (the GDGS pattern); receiving needs custom dyno shader work.

Verdict: a library of 30-270 splat instances is not realistic on phones at photoreal quality. It is technically feasible on desktop at the demo-bed scale.
routes.risks:
- Lighting mismatch with the sun, HDRI and shadows: the main realism giveaway.
- Missing from Photo mode unless a raster-over-path-trace composite is built.
- 910 KB gzip extra download.
- Phone memory and fill-rate.
- MSAA cost.
- Glass-railing sort artefacts.
- Large per-species downloads (about 2-5 MB each).
- Spark API churn (0.1 to 2.0 migration; 2.1 to 2.3.1 between May and October 2026).

routes.name: R8. Recommended hybrid: captured atlases on generated geometry, with splat- and photo-derived references and impostors
routes.what:
One programme combining the strengths of R1-R6:
1. R1 atlases from every species give the leaf, needle, petal and bark appearance.
2. R2 multi-angle photos and optional R6 splats of 2-3 specimens per species supply measured crown envelopes, card density and clump structure for the procedural generator, plus side-by-side photo-match QA at the Corner, Front and bed close-up cameras.
3. LOD2 hemi-octahedral impostors are baked from the finished LOD0, which keeps them relightable with normals, or from splat renders.
4. R3/R4 photogrammetry is used only for bark, trunk flares and clipped-evergreen base shells.
5. Splats are not used at runtime in v1.

Rollout: a 3-4 species pilot now (Smaragd, boxwood, Karl Foerster, blue spruce), the rest of the evergreens and grasses this autumn and winter, and deciduous summer looks and blooms in May-August 2027.
routes.species_coverage:
Capturable now (October 2026, before hard frost):
- Full capture: white pine, blue spruce, Smaragd, yew, boxwood.
- Autumn form: Karl Foerster, little bluestem, switchgrass.
- Autumn-colour variants: sugar maple, red maple, serviceberry, redbud, red-osier dogwood, spirea, ninebark, lilac.
- Seed-head or dried-head looks: coneflower, Rudbeckia, bergamot, Annabelle, panicle hydrangea, ostrich fern (fertile fronds).
- Bark of all trees.

Winter (Nov-Mar): leaf-off branching of the maples, serviceberry, redbud and lilac; dogwood red stems; ninebark bark.

Spring 2027:
- Serviceberry bloom, late April to early May.
- Redbud bloom, mid-May.
- Lilac bloom, mid to late May.

June 2027 (summer leaves and early blooms):
- Summer leaves of all deciduous species.
- Hosta, before slug damage.
- Ostrich fern fronds.
- First flush of catmint and salvia.
- Ninebark and spirea flowers.
- Karl Foerster pink plumes.

July-August 2027 (summer blooms):
- Coneflower and Rudbeckia flowers.
- Bergamot flowers; shoot early, before mildew.
- Daylily flowers.
- Annabelle white heads.
- Panicle hydrangea white or lime heads.
- Switchgrass panicles.
- Little bluestem blue foliage.
- Salvia rebloom.

Hosta and daylily summer foliage cannot be captured until June 2027; both are already yellowing. All 26 species are covered at species or cultivar level by August 2027.
routes.realism: This is the realistic path to 'cannot tell from a photo' in path-traced Photo-mode stills and at Corner and Front distances. Every texel is a real photograph of the exact species, and the geometry is fitted to measured real specimens and checked against reference photos from the same camera. Real-time phone views will be clearly better than today, but not indistinguishable; no surveyed method achieves that on phone budgets. The quality bar and precedents are Megascans (https://80.lv/articles/billy-lundevall-creating-content-for-megascans) and the R1 and R2 examples. Use the photo-match test as the acceptance gate instead of a subjective review.
routes.licence:
All shipped pixels and geometry are project-owned (Golden Maple copyright). Tools used are free and licence-clean:
- darktable GPL-3.0; Meshroom MPL-2.0; COLMAP BSD-3.
- RealityScan: free under US$1M group revenue; EULA §6 'does not grant to Licensor any right, title, or interest in any of the content that you produce'.
- Brush and gsplat Apache-2.0; SuperSplat MIT; octahedral-impostor MIT; BiRefNet MIT.

Excluded as non-commercial or encumbered: rembg's default bria-rmbg, INRIA 3DGS/2DGS/SuGaR, Postshot Free, Metashape trial/demo, Depth Anything V2 Base and Large.

Shipping: derived assets can be committed to the public repo with a rights notice, or served from a separate origin. RAW masters stay private and off the repo.
routes.cost:
- Gear: about C$350-700 one-time (R1 and R2 lists; each purchase needs owner approval).
- Software: $0 on the free path. US$1,250/yr only if over RealityScan's threshold. Optional Metashape Standard US$179.
- Plants: $0 if captured from stock already bought for client jobs; otherwise nursery purchases need approval (estimate C$15-150 per plant).
- Owner time (estimate): about 45-70 h of shooting over October 2026 to August 2027, plus review of the photo-match sheets.
- Pipeline build and processing: about 1-2 h per species once the scripts exist.
routes.owner_actions:
1. Approve the pilot and its gear now; the frost window is closing.
2. Confirm revenue against the RealityScan threshold.
3. Get nursery permission (Connon Waterdown, Sheridan) and client consent for job-site captures. This is outreach, so it is the owner's to do.
4. Pick the representative cultivars.
5. Approve installs: darktable, Meshroom, RealityScan, Brush, Blender.
6. Choose the asset rights notice.
7. Set the default render season (summer) and decide whether autumn variants ship.
8. Book the 2027 sessions: late April to May blooms, June foliage, July to August blooms.
routes.web_fit:
Runtime stays plain three.js meshes, with no new runtime dependency:
- LOD0: tree 15-25k tris; shrub 2-8k; perennial 1-4k.
- LOD1: about one third of LOD0.
- LOD2: 2-triangle octahedral impostor, the constrained-tier default.
- Shared 1k-2k KTX2 atlases, about 0.5-1.5 MB per species (estimate). Everything sits in the existing lazy Landscape3D chunk.

Compatibility: MSAA alpha-to-coverage, GTAO, shadow maps, Neutral tone mapping, and the path tracer with LOD0 forced for all 273 showcase plants.

Build-side tools needed:
- KTX2 encoder.
- gltf-transform or meshoptimizer.
- An impostor baker.
- An updated check-landscape-objects.ts that accepts project-owned provenance: date, location type, photographer, ColorChecker reference.

Saved designs pick models by species at render time, so no data migration is needed.
routes.risks:
- Season dependency: deciduous summer looks only from June 2027, so interim assets must remain.
- Owner time and weather: wind, rain, early frost.
- The geometry craft still decides the final look; the capture removes the texture and species errors but not the modelling work.
- Colour consistency across a year of sessions: one ColorChecker and fixed lighting presets.
- Mislabelled nursery cultivars.
- Privacy: EXIF GPS, and client homes appearing in job-site frames.
- Storage: about 50-100 GB of masters off the repo, keeping C: free space above the 10 GB alert threshold.
- If the pilot's photo-match fails, revisit paid curated libraries; those were outside this sweep.
